items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had known Kenny from playing two dates with him, with Dizzy and Yusef.

ctx.x: Because everybody else was a few years older. Roland was like that one year too late … for …
Yeah. And Paul, and Kenny Burrell, Yusef Lateef, and Curtis …Curtis Fuller and Louis Hayes and … they'd all gone on to New York before I even got to visit the clubs in New York.
Okay. So '55, you're off to Eastman, you do your first year, you come back, you work summers …

items.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I put together Ron Carter and Jim Hall to come in. That was the first time they worked together, I was responsible for that getting together.

ctx.x: Sometimes I played there solo, sometimes I played there duo. I was mostly solos and duos. I started booking other people in there. I brought in my friend from Washington D.C. Bill Harris, guitarist, to play solo. Did I mention Larry Ridley, I think I just did. No, I didn't. He played bass with me in the duo settings. Then I put together a couple of combinations. I put together Ron Carter and Jim Hall to come in. That was the first time they worked together, I was responsible for that getting together. A couple of…
